planting.note: Set out rooted cuttings/plugs after frost danger passes; this first-year-flowering color joins the compact, well-matched Honeysticks series.

directions: This Honeysticks color produces upright spikes of bright golden-yellow tubular flowers with hints of orange above aromatic, anise-scented foliage. It flowers in its first year from a compact, strongly branching plant bred to stay in scale with the other Honeysticks colors for combination planting. Bees and other pollinators are drawn readily to the spikes, and the plant holds up to Zone 4 winters once established. Grow in full sun with lean to average, well-drained soil, since good drainage matters more than fertility for keeping this hyssop compact and long-lived.
sources: Dümmen Orange (dummenorange.com) — Honeysticks Gold product page, CAST 2026 press release

planting.note: Plant rooted cuttings after frost danger passes; new bicolor addition to the bee-friendly, single-flowered Summer Bees series.

directions: Salmon Bicolor brings peach-and-orange single flowers with a yellow, star-shaped center to the Summer Bees dahlia series, a line specifically bred with open, pollen-accessible blooms that bees and other pollinators can easily work. The plant carries a naturally vigorous, well-branched, upright habit and has shown good mildew resistance, a trait being carried forward into future Summer Bees colors. It suits in-ground landscape plantings as well as 6-inch-and-larger containers, and works equally well as a solo specimen or combination component. Treat as a tender, cutting-grown plant set out after frost danger has passed, in full sun with evenly moist, well-drained soil.
sources: Dümmen Orange (dummenorange.com) — Summer Bees Salmon Bicolor product page

planting.note: Plant rooted cuttings/plugs after frost danger passes; an Intrinsa-powered, 2026 Retailers' Choice Award-winning introduction.

directions: Violet Vortex combines violet and soft cream petals in a swirling, tricolor pattern on a medium, upright plant with early, dependable flowering. It was recognized with a Retailers' Choice Award at Cultivate'26 for its distinctive bloom pattern and reliable garden performance under variable weather. The variety is grown on Dümmen Orange's Intrinsa rootstock platform, bred for improved disease resistance and production consistency. Grow in full sun in containers, hanging baskets, or mixed combination plantings with consistently moist, well-drained soil.
sources: Dümmen Orange (dummenorange.com) — Sweetunia Violet Vortex product page

planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants in spring; fills containers faster than other black-foliage heucheras and is day-length neutral.

directions: Everglow Midnight is among the closest selections yet to a true black-leaf heuchera, with rounded, high-gloss, near-black purple foliage forming a compact, evergreen-to-semi-evergreen mound. It fills out a pot faster than comparable dark-leaved coral bells and tolerates both sun and shade, though foliage color and gloss hold up best with afternoon shade in hot climates and some morning sun in cooler ones. The deep, glossy color works as a solo landscape accent or as a foil that makes brighter companion colors pop in mixed containers. Plant in fertile, well-drained soil with steady moisture; it is reliably hardy to Zone 4.
sources: Darwin Perennials (darwinperennials.com) — Heuchera Everglow Midnight product page

common_name: Sombrero Poco Hot Pink Improved Coneflower

planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants in spring for same-year bloom; a compact Poco-series dwarf form of the Sombrero coneflower line.

directions: This improved Poco-series selection keeps the dwarf, sturdy habit of the Sombrero Poco coneflower line but with richer, more saturated hot-pink blooms than the earlier release it replaces. Plants stay compact and heavily branched, producing abundant flat daisy-form flowers from late spring through late summer that draw butterflies while resisting deer browsing. The exceptionally hardy, well-branched habit makes it reliable in the landscape and quick to finish in production. Grow in full sun in well-drained, average soil; it tolerates heat and summer dryness once established.
sources: Darwin Perennials (darwinperennials.com) — Echinacea Sombrero Poco Hot Pink Improved product page

planting.note: Plant container-grown divisions in spring in gritty, sharply drained soil; part of the SunBurst series bred for larger, more abundant early-spring flowers.

directions: SunBurst Rose produces masses of small, five-petaled, rose-pink flowers resembling miniature roses over a dense mat of silvery-green foliage in early-to-late spring. It is bred to carry larger, more numerous blooms than older sun rose varieties while keeping the classic low, spreading, drought-tolerant habit that thrives in poor, rocky soil. The tough, low-maintenance plant attracts bees and butterflies, resists deer browsing, and tolerates light frost. Grow in full sun with excellent drainage, watering lightly and allowing the soil to dry between waterings since it is intolerant of wet feet.
sources: Darwin Perennials (darwinperennials.com) — Helianthemum nummularium SunBurst Rose product page
